clue.text: Motion follows test supporter's sound academic qualification

indicators.note: follows puts the poet's title after the earlier pieces in the answer

parts.note: a test match is an international game, as in cricket or rugby

indicators.note: sound tells us to take how the supporter's word is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a supporter is a backer, someone who funds or champions a cause
Andrew Motion was Britain's Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: A debating motion comes after a cricket fan's sensible remarks about exam results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' looks like a proposal in a debate, but it stands for the poet Andrew Motion, so it gives his title, LAUREATE. 'sound' means BACKER said aloud, written BACCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The International Baccalaureate is a school-leaving diploma taken worldwide, a kind of academic qualification.

clue.text: Stimulant for 1116-0 crash in semi-nuanced case

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled numerals inside the half-word that serves as their case
semi- means half, so take the first half of the word nuanced
crash suggests a smash-up, so the Roman numerals and the zero are jumbled

parts.note: 1116 in Roman numerals is MCXVI
a zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A drug blamed for a cricket collapse of 1116 for none, tucked in a subtle casing.
explanation.walkthrough: '1116-0' reads like a cricket score, but it is Roman numerals plus a zero. The half-word from 'semi' acts as the case that 'in' fills with the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nux vomica is the seed of a tree that gives strychnine, used in small doses as a stimulant tonic.

clue.text: Girl in cartel lending money

indicators.note: in says the name sits inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A girl is caught up in a cartel's money-lending business.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's first name, and crosswords often use girl for any such name.

clue.text: First person in France to follow bit of navy painting with a little orange

indicators.note: to follow puts the French word after the other pieces
a bit of the word navy is its first letter only

parts.note: taken as written
painting is a form of art
je is French for I, the first person singular

explanation.surface: A French speaker comes after a bit of naval art showing a small orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First person in France' looks like a Frenchman, but it is the French pronoun for I. A naartje is South African English, from Afrikaans.
explanation.definitionFit: A naartje is the South African name for a tangerine, a small citrus fruit like a little orange.

clue.text: Felt shy revealing Pope's recommended object of knowledge

indicators.note: revealing suggests the two words open up to show a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone feels bashful about exposing what a poet told us to study.
explanation.walkthrough: Alexander Pope wrote 'Know then thyself', echoing the ancient 'know thyself'; 'revealing' rearranges FELT SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope's Essay on Man urges us to know ourselves before presuming to study God, so the self is what he recommends knowing.

clue.text: To put up a lot of herb (sage) in a different style

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word herb, losing its final letter

parts.note: a sage is a wise person, and sage as an adjective means wise

explanation.surface: A recipe tells you to hang up most of a herb, sage, in a new way.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'put up' reads upwards. The brackets round 'sage' make it look like the herb in question, but here it is the adjective meaning clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in another way or manner, matching in a different style.

clue.text: Wholly committed to suffering exhaustion

definitions.meaning: an ... deal or bet stakes everything, holding nothing back
someone who is ... is worn out, completely tired

explanation.definitionFit: All in means both everything included or staked and, informally, utterly exhausted.

clue.text: See 1
See 26
Supporter wants gold for team needing 50 for record, not 500

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a football or cricket team
L is fifty in Roman numerals

indicators.note: not removes the five hundred from the word for a record

parts.note: a diary is a daily record
D is five hundred in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A fan wants a gold medal for a team needing fifty runs for a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes D (500) from DIARY to leave IARY.
explanation.definitionFit: An auxiliary is a helper or supporting worker, giving extra support.

clue.text: Old coin for Goldie — about turn for Cal

indicators.note: about puts the actress's surname around the other letters

parts.note: Goldie Hawn is an American film actress

indicators.note: turn makes the letters of the two words rotate into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is asking about an actress making a U-turn on behalf of California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about turn' looks like an about-face, one military order, but 'about' is the container signal and 'turn' the anagram signal, working separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The half-crown was a British coin worth two shillings and sixpence, withdrawn in 1970.

clue.text: See 11
It comes, as push to shove, when apothecary centre has to manage church

definitions.text: It comes, as push to shove

indicators.note: centre takes the middle four letters of the word apothecary

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's shop at the heart of town is told to run the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes THEC, the middle four letters of APOTHECARY. The definition plays on the saying 'when push comes to shove'.
explanation.definitionFit: The crunch is the decisive moment, which arrives just as the idiom says when push comes to shove.

clue.text: Retreat for a time to cattle market shelter

parts.note: a lair is a hidden den or retreat
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone retreats for a while to a shed at the cattle market.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairage is a place where cattle are rested on the way to market or slaughter, a kind of shelter.

clue.text: Belly laugh starts after rating for Latin mistress

indicators.note: after puts the laugh's opening after the other pieces

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
domina is Latin for a mistress or lady

indicators.note: starts takes only the first letter of the word laugh

explanation.surface: A belly laugh begins after a sailor stands in for the Latin teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belly laugh' reads as one phrase, but 'Belly' is the definition. 'Latin mistress' looks like a teacher; it is the Latin word for mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdominal is the adjective for the belly, as in abdominal muscles, so it means belly used before a noun.

clue.text: Hand for one who loses it?

definitions.meaning: a hand is informally called a ...
to flip is to lose your temper, so this is someone who flips

explanation.definitionFit: Flipper is slang for a hand and, playfully, one who flips or goes into a rage.

clue.text: Eye fastening for curtain, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is to be taken as it sounds

parts.note: a pin is a fastening, joined here to the word curtain

explanation.surface: A clue asks what fastens a curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eye' looks like a curtain eyelet, but it is a private eye. PIN plus CURTAIN, said aloud, sounds like the name of the famous detective agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinkerton's was the famous American detective agency, so a Pinkerton is a private eye.

clue.text: It's abandoned Nehru to his end in Uttar Pradesh — keep climbing on it

annotationWithheld.why: It's abandoned Nehru to his end in Uttar Pradesh (2,3,2): PAND (PANDIT, Nehru's title, minus IT) plus U inside UP, but U is the end of Nehru, so Nehru gives PANDIT and is also the source of U, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: It's abandoned Nehru to his end in Uttar Pradesh — keep climbing on it

clue.text: Indian making quiet thrust into higher education?

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

indicators.note: into puts the thrust inside the word for university

parts.note: uni, short for university, is higher education
a jab is a quick thrust

explanation.surface: A quiet push to get into university.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi is a person from the Punjab region of India, so an Indian.

clue.text: Row about nose job giving judges a holiday?

indicators.note: about puts the word for row around the other letters

parts.note: a din is a loud row or racket

indicators.note: job, as in a nose job, signals that the letters of nose are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fuss over cosmetic surgery means the judges get a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nose job' reads as cosmetic surgery, but 'job' is the anagram signal on 'nose'. 'Row' is a noisy quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Dies non is a legal term for a day on which no court business is done, a holiday for judges.

clue.text: Gadabout outside topless tower going on for 24 hours?

indicators.note: outside puts the reversed word round the shortened tower
about turns the word gad round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: topless removes the first letter of the word for the tower

parts.note: a pylon is a tall tower carrying power lines

explanation.surface: A gadabout walks round a tower whose top has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gadabout' reads as one word for a restless person, but split it: 'Gad' then 'about', which turns it round. The question mark admits that a long day is not quite 24 hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylong means lasting all day, roughly a full day of twenty-four hours.

clue.text: Not much interest in exchange for old rope?

definitions.meaning: loans at low interest rates are called cheap or ...
the saying money for old rope means pay earned for almost no effort

explanation.definitionFit: Easy money means both credit at low interest and money earned with almost no effort.

clue.text: Sacred melody takes flight

parts.note: St, saint, is an abbreviation linked to sacred things
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.definitionFit: A stair can mean a whole flight of steps, as in going up the stair.

clue.text: Players in tune with puff for nostalgia?

indicators.note: in puts the players inside the tune

parts.note: a strain is a tune or passage of music
a team is a group of players

explanation.surface: Musicians in tune breathing out for old times' sake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puff' looks like breath, but it is a puffer, a childish word for a train, now kept running mainly for nostalgia.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam train, a puffer, is now run mostly on heritage lines for nostalgia.

clue.text: Move to get something to wear

explanation.definitionFit: Shift means both to move and a straight loose dress.

clue.text: See 23
Samson's past wrongdoing brought back when group brought back

parts.note: ago means in the past

indicators.note: brought back turns the word for wrongdoing round

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing

indicators.note: brought back again turns the word for group round

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A biblical strongman's old sins return when his gang comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns SIN into NIS, and the second 'brought back' turns SET into TES. Samson Agonistes is Milton's verse drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's poem is Samson Agonistes, so the word completes Samson's title; it means the struggler.

clue.text: So long, singer! As hormonal test shows, such as Mick won't get such as Kate

definitions.text: such as Mick won't get such as Kate

indicators.note: shows suggests the result of the test appears, so these letters are rearranged

parts.words: So long, singer! As hormonal test

explanation.surface: A singer is waved off as a hormone test reveals a rock star won't land a supermodel.
explanation.walkthrough: Mick Jagger is a Rolling Stone and Kate Moss a model, so the definition spells out the proverb word by word. 'shows' rearranges the twenty-six letters of the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a restless person never settles; here a Rolling Stone does not gather a Moss, playing on Jagger and Kate Moss.
